common_text: Master-at-Arms (MA) will, individually or as part of a force, conduct Force Protection (FP) - Antiterrorism (AT), Physical Security (PS), and Law Enforcement (LE) - operations in order to defeat threats at-sea, on-shore, and in expeditionary environments: conduct scalable FP and security, providing layered defense for designated assets and critical infrastructure throughout the world; operate in an integrated sea/coastal/landward security environment, providing mobile and fixed defensive operations while organizing and training their personnel in AT, PS, LE, and weapons proficiency in support of Commanders performing base defense, Naval Criminal Investigative Services (NCIS) operations, expeditionary/combat operations, strategic asset security, LE, corrections, and special events and operations with other services to include harbor security and Military Working Dog (MWD) operations, host nation partners, and civil authorities. __________________________________

Master-at-Arms (MA) will, individually or as part of a force, conduct Force Protection (FP) - Antiterrorism (AT), Physical Security (PS), and Law Enforcement (LE) - operations in order to defeat threats at-sea, on-shore, and in expeditionary environments: conduct scalable FP and security, providing layered defense for designated assets and critical infrastructure throughout the world; operate in an integrated sea/coastal/landward security environment, providing mobile and fixed defensive operations while organizing and training their personnel in AT, PS, LE, and weapons proficiency in support of Commanders performing base defense, Naval Criminal Investigative Services (NCIS) operations, expeditionary/combat operations, strategic asset security, LE, corrections, and special events and operations with other services to include harbor security and Military Working Dog (MWD) operations, host nation partners, and civil authorities. __________________________________

Strategic Asset Security Specialists provide protection and continual physical security of the Nation’s nuclear forces while assigned to Fleet Air Reconnaissance Squadron (VQ) Take Charge and Move Out (TACAMO) and/or Marine Corps Security Force Battalions (MCSFB) at Strategic Weapons Facilities (SWF): perform Nuclear Weapons Security (NWS) operations; perform TACAMO operations as members of Strategic Communications Wing One, Fleet Air Reconnaissance Squadrons and U.S. Strategic Command (USSTRATCOM) Airborne National Command Posts; and serve in Priority 1 Chief of Naval Operations (CNO) and Manning Control Authorities (MCA) assignments.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
